description: Kanhe protocol objects of specification revision v0.18 (where a record came from: scripts and sources), built by an independent Python encoder (tools/testvectors/provenance_vectors.py, with generate.py's) from spec/README.md (sections 5, 6, and 11) and spec/kanhe.cddl. Times are milliseconds since the epoch. `mechanism_types` lists the seven mechanism types in the specification's table order. `script_metadata` holds script metadata (record key 5 of a kanhe.script/1 record) on its own: `valid` cases, each its deterministic CBOR and its values (digests in hex, runtime null when absent), the specification's example first; `refused` cases, each breaking the one rule that `why` names: "no metadata" (not a map), "unknown key", "missing key", and the key or file part whose rule is broken: "name", "version", "files" (not 1 to 256), "file" (not [path, size, digest]), "path", "size", "digest" (not 32 bytes), "order" (paths not strictly ascending by bytes), "deterministic", "runtime". `source_statuses` holds where a source stood at given times (section 11, step 10): its registration time, when it was revoked and replaced (null if never), and cases of a time `t` and the status then: "not_yet", "revoked", "replaced", or "live", in that order of precedence. `replay` holds a bank's log for each hash, in the format of protocol-v0.16.json's ledgers: the organization (Example Bank) registers a person with a passkey and a hardware key (user-verified) and a device, and delegates to each; the person approves scripts in person; the device registers records naming a script in their provenance (key 5) and sources (key 7), on this ledger and another. `refused` statements are validated against the state after the first `after` statements, at `at`, and break exactly one rule, which `why` names: "in person" (a script's registration without a person's user-verified proof of presence), the script metadata rules above, "mechanism" (a mechanism type names sources), "not a script", "no such script", "withdrawn" (provenance naming a record that is not a script, none, or a revoked script), "no such source", "mechanism source", "superseded source", "revoked source" (a local source missing, of a mechanism type, superseded, or revoked), "role" (a script takes no endorsement), "revoked" (a revoked record takes nothing more). `malformed` statements do not parse, for the CDDL rule `why` names. A registration is a statement about its own record only: a source's and a script's histories do not change when a record names them. `records` gives each record's type, state, revocation, registrant, history, versions, sources (ledger and record ids), the script its registration's provenance names, and, for a script, its values. `log_entries` holds the whole log, ending with the state commitment over `state_leaves`; `checkpoint` (signed at `checkpoint_time`) covers it; keys are seed = SHA-256("Kanhe test key: v0.18 <name>"), `seeds`. Evidence bundles with scripts and sources are made by the reference implementation's tests, which both verifiers must report alike.

refused.name: a key that is not text
a version that is a number

statements.name: genesis
register the risk officer, a person
register the officer's passkey and hardware key
delegate scripts, loan books, and reports to the officer
register the risk engine, a device
delegate loan books and reports to the risk engine
the officer approves risk-model 3.2 with the hardware key
the risk engine registers the November loan book
the risk engine registers the monthly report, by the script, from the loan book and the exchange's rate table
the risk engine registers the December loan book
and a corrected version of it
the organization revokes the November loan book: a figure was wrong
the risk engine registers another report from the corrected book, by the script
the officer withdraws risk-model 3.2
the officer approves risk-model 3.3 with a passkey that verified them

refused.name: approve a script without proof of presence
approve a script with a passkey that did not verify the person
the organization approves a script (no person)
a script whose metadata has an unknown key
a script whose files are out of order
a report naming a loan book as its script
a report naming a script that does not exist
a report from a local source that does not exist
a report from the script as its source (a mechanism type)
a report from the replaced December book
a report from the revoked November book
a report by the withdrawn script

malformed.name: a source list that is empty
a source whose record is 31 bytes
a provenance key the CDDL does not name
